§ 1402. Definitions. For purposes of computing net earnings from self-employment, every
individual carrying on a trade or business, other than as an employee, must include the
distributive share of income or loss from such trade or business in gross income. Net earnings
from self-employment are subject to self-employment tax at the rate set by section 1401,
covering the equivalent of both the employer and employee shares of Social Security and
Medicare, up to the contribution and benefit base for the taxable year, plus the Medicare
portion above that base without limit, per 26 U.S.C. § 1402.

§ 911. Citizens or residents of the United States living abroad. A qualified individual may
elect to exclude from gross income the foreign earned income exclusion amount for the taxable
year, adjusted annually for inflation, provided the individual satisfies either the bona fide
residence test or the physical presence test described in IRC § 911(d). Housing cost amounts in
excess of the base housing amount may also qualify for exclusion or deduction under this
section.
